prompt: My blue colour is ignored because another rule with an id selector sets it to red.
tells: another rule with an id selector
why: An id selector is more specific than a class, so it wins. That's specificity.
trap: Load order matters only when specificity ties.

prompt: Two rules with the same selector set different fonts, and the one further down the file wins.
tells: the one further down the file wins
why: When specificity ties, the later rule wins. That's the cascade.
trap: It isn't about scripts; it's CSS order.

prompt: Someone added !important to force a style, and now nothing else can override it.
why: !important jumps the cascade, which makes later changes hard.
trap: It isn't layout; it's which rule wins.

prompt: Setting the font on body made every paragraph use it too.
tells: made every paragraph use it too
why: Some properties pass down from parent to children. That's part of the cascade.
trap: The DOM tree makes it possible, but the clue is inherited styles.

prompt: A style written directly on the element beats the stylesheet.
tells: written directly on the element beats the stylesheet
why: Inline styles are more specific than stylesheet rules.
trap: JavaScript might set them, but the clue is which style wins.

prompt: DevTools shows the rule crossed out because a more specific one overrides it.
tells: a more specific one overrides it
why: Crossed-out rules lost in the cascade.
trap: Size and layout aren't the issue; which rule applies is.
